turns.question: What does Section 11-134 say about the annuity formula?
turns.answer:
Section 11-134 provides several annuity formulas. The main formula for withdrawals on or after January 1, 2002 is **2.40% of final average salary for each year of service**, with final average salary based on the highest average annual salary for any **4 consecutive years within the last 10 years of service**. The general maximum is **80% of final average salary**. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

If the annuity begins before age 60, the section generally provides a reduction of **0.25% for each full month or fractional part of a month** that the annuity-starting age is below 60. Exceptions apply for certain service levels and retirement ages. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

The section also includes a separate election for an annuity beginning no earlier than age 60, available to an employee with at least 10 years of service. That election uses the same 2.40%-per-year formula for withdrawals on or after January 1, 2002, but the Code does not provide enough information here to determine which formula would produce the larger annuity for you. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

Your 21.5 years of service is governed for minimum-annuity purposes by the service-credit rules in Section 11-216. Those rules include special counting rules for minimum annuities, including the rule that service during 6 or more months in a year constitutes a year of service. [40 ILCS 5/11-216]

The statute sections available here do not establish your final average salary, intended annuity starting date, or the effect of any service or leave history. I also could not establish matters that depend on Sections 11-221 or 11-164, which are referenced but not provided.

turns.question: What does Article 22A of the Pension Code provide?

Article 22A establishes the Illinois State Board of Investment and governs the investment management of certain retirement-system assets. The sections read here refer to that Board and to commingled investment funds established under Article 22A. [40 ILCS 5/16-179.1] [40 ILCS 5/15-167.1]

It does not set pension eligibility, service-credit rules, retirement ages, or annuity amounts. Those matters are governed by the Article covering the particular retirement system. Fiduciaries must act solely in participants’ and beneficiaries’ interests, provide benefits and pay reasonable administrative expenses, use care and prudence, diversify investments, and follow the applicable Article.
